title: Repair run changed nothing — all five defects named in FEEDBACK.md are still present
evidence: TASK.md is a REPAIR TASK and FEEDBACK.md lists 'POST /books not exposed', 'GET /books/{id} not exposed', 'PUT /books/{id} not exposed', 'DELETE /books/{id} not exposed', 'No input validation'. grep -rn -E '@app\.|@router\.|APIRouter|include_router' --include='*.py' . returns exactly 2 hits: main.py:22 @app.get("/health") and main.py:26 @app.get("/books"). retort.db run 11 has _second_try=1.0, _turns=12, _duration_seconds=41.5.
suggestion: Wire book_api.py's existing CRUD functions into main.py as FastAPI routes; the logic is already written.

title: All 8 tests in test_book_api.py fail — every HTTP request raises before its assert
evidence: Archived .coverage line_bits for test_book_api.py cover the request-issuing lines (18, 23-27, 37, 45-49, 64-68, 88-92, 106-110, 125) but NONE of the assert lines that immediately follow (19, 29, 38, 51, 70, 94, 112, 126). book_api.py and main.py have ZERO covered lines, so application code was never executed. Stored test_coverage=0.25 is whole-directory line coverage carried entirely by the test files.
suggestion: Start the server via a fixture with a readiness poll (or use fastapi.testclient.TestClient) instead of a bare module-level subprocess.Popen + sleep(2).

title: GET /books route exists but its table is never created — 500 on a fresh workspace
evidence: main.py:26-33 SELECTs from books, but main.py:7 init_db() is defined and never called (grep init_db -> only book_api.py:143 calls book_api's own copy; no @app.on_event/lifespan anywhere). No books.db exists in the archive, so the first request raises sqlite3.OperationalError: no such table: books. The route also returns raw tuples (main.py:31-33), not JSON objects.
suggestion: Call init_db() at startup and return dicts built from cursor.description.

title: POST /books is not exposed by the served app
evidence: No @app.post anywhere (grep over all *.py returns 0 hits). book_api.py:24 create_book(title, author, year, isbn) is a complete, correct implementation but main.py:1-2 imports only fastapi and sqlite3 and never imports book_api.

title: GET /books ignores the ?author= filter
evidence: main.py:27 'async def get_books()' takes no parameters and main.py:30 runs an unconditional 'SELECT * FROM books'. The filtering logic exists at book_api.py:42-55 (get_all_books(author=...)) but is unrouted.
suggestion: Add an 'author: Optional[str] = None' query parameter and delegate to book_api.get_all_books.

title: GET /books/{id} is not exposed by the served app
evidence: No path-parameter route exists — the only two decorators in the workspace are main.py:22 and main.py:26. book_api.py:57 get_book_by_id() is unrouted, so nothing can return the 404 the spec requires.
suggestion: Add @app.get('/books/{book_id}') raising HTTPException(404) when get_book_by_id returns None.

title: PUT /books/{id} is not exposed by the served app
evidence: No @app.put decorator anywhere (grep over all *.py returns 0 hits). book_api.py:70-112 update_book() is a complete implementation but is never imported or routed.

title: DELETE /books/{id} is not exposed by the served app
evidence: No @app.delete decorator anywhere (grep over all *.py returns 0 hits). book_api.py:114-131 delete_book() is unrouted.

title: No HTTP status codes other than the implicit 200 are ever produced
evidence: grep -rn -E 'HTTPException|status_code|JSONResponse' over application code returns 0 hits in main.py and book_api.py (only test assertions match). The spec's 201/400/404/204 paths do not exist; book_api.py:40 raises a bare Exception for a duplicate ISBN, which would surface as a 500, not a 400.
suggestion: Use status_code= on the route decorators and raise fastapi.HTTPException for error cases.

title: No input validation — title and author are never enforced at the request boundary
evidence: No pydantic BaseModel or request body model exists anywhere (grep BaseModel|pydantic returns 0 hits). With no POST route there is no place a 400 could be returned. book_api.py:24's required positional args are Python-level only.
suggestion: Define a pydantic BookCreate model with required title/author so FastAPI returns 422/400 automatically.

title: 10 tests exist and run, but 8 fail and the 2 that pass assert nothing
evidence: Stored test_coverage=0.25 (>0, so tests executed). test_book_api.py's 8 tests all fail (see finding test-fail-all). The 2 passing tests, test_db.py:7 test_database and test_simple.py:6 test_database, contain zero 'assert' statements — they are print-only sqlite smoke scripts that pass unconditionally.
suggestion: Replace the print-only scripts with assertions against the real API surface.

title: The only two passing tests contain no assertions and are near-duplicates of each other
evidence: test_db.py:7-38 and test_simple.py:6-48 both open a local sqlite file, insert rows, print counts, and unlink the file. Neither file contains the token 'assert'. They exercise sqlite itself, not book_api.py or main.py (both of which have 0 covered lines in .coverage).
suggestion: Delete one and convert the other into an assertion-bearing test of book_api's functions.

title: Prompt instruction not followed: tests do not demonstrate the implementation meets the requirements
evidence: prompts/neutral.md asks to 'include tests that demonstrate the implementation meets the requirements'. The tests that target the requirements (test_book_api.py) all fail, and the tests that pass never touch main.py or book_api.py (0 covered lines in .coverage for both).
suggestion: Make the API tests pass against the served app.

title: README documents five endpoints that the served app does not implement
evidence: README.md 'API Endpoints' lists GET /books/{id}, POST /books, PUT /books/{id}, DELETE /books/{id} and gives curl examples for all of them, but only GET /health and GET /books exist (main.py:22, main.py:26). The README also has three unterminated backticks and a 'http://http://localhost:8000' typo in the PUT example.
suggestion: Either implement the endpoints or correct the README to describe what actually ships.

title: test_book_api.py spawns uvicorn at import time with a fixed sleep and never reaps it
evidence: test_book_api.py:10 calls subprocess.Popen([...]) at module scope, followed by time.sleep(2) at line 13. There is no readiness check, no fixture, and no teardown, so the process leaks and collection-time failure is indistinguishable from test failure. 'import time' appears twice (lines 5 and 7).
suggestion: Use a pytest fixture with a readiness poll and terminate the process on teardown, or switch to TestClient.

title: init_db and the books schema are duplicated across two modules
evidence: main.py:7-20 and book_api.py:8-22 define byte-identical init_db() functions with the same CREATE TABLE statement (both with the same mis-indented closing '"""' at main.py:18 / book_api.py:20).
suggestion: Keep one definition in book_api.py and import it into main.py.

title: get_book_by_id reads cursor.description after the connection is closed
evidence: book_api.py:63 calls conn.close(), then book_api.py:66 reads cursor.description to build the column list. Using a cursor whose connection has been closed is not contractually safe in sqlite3.

title: Scratch file check_env.py left in the deliverable
evidence: check_env.py:1-4 only prints sys.version and sys.path[0]; it is not referenced by any other file and is unrelated to the task.
